headline_marked: Iran claims [[85 US military sites hit]] in Bahrain and Kuwait
headline: Iran claims 85 US military sites hit in Bahrain and Kuwait
summary: The IRGC says the missile and drone strikes were a 'primary response' to recent US attacks on Iranian soil.
details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have launched joint missile and drone attacks on 85 US military installations across Bahrain and Kuwait.
The IRGC stated that the operation, carried out by its naval and air forces, targeted the US Navy's Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain and the Ali Al-Salem airbase in Kuwait.

This action is described as a 'primary response' to US strikes on Tuesday night in the Iranian port cities of Sirik, Bandar Abbas, and Qeshm Island, which the US alleged were linked to attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
The IRGC further alleged that Washington timed these attacks to overshadow the funeral and farewell ceremonies of Iran's late supreme leader.
While Iran's top joint military command has vowed a 'devastating response,' the IRGC has not provided specific details on casualties or the extent of the damage caused by these strikes.
The US government has not yet issued an official response to Iran's claims of the attacks.
Analysts warn that this cycle of retaliatory strikes between the two powers could further destabilize regional security and risk a wider conflict in the Middle East.

This action is described as a 'primary response' to US strikes on Tuesday night in the Iranian port cities of Sirik, Bandar Abbas, and Qeshm Island, which the US alleged were linked to attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC further alleged that Washington timed these attacks to overshadow the funeral and farewell ceremonies of Iran's late supreme leader.

While Iran's top joint military command has vowed a 'devastating response,' the IRGC has not provided specific details on casualties or the extent of the damage caused by these strikes.

The US government has not yet issued an official response to Iran's claims of the attacks.

Analysts warn that this cycle of retaliatory strikes between the two powers could further destabilize regional security and risk a wider conflict in the Middle East.

headline_marked: Messi penalty miss sparks clash: [[Man killed in Cumilla]] over football dispute
headline: Messi penalty miss sparks clash: Man killed in Cumilla over football dispute
summary: A 35-year-old man was fatally injured during a violent clash between football supporters at a tea stall in Cumilla.
details: A 35-year-old man, identified as Md Shariful Islam, was killed after a dispute among football supporters escalated into violence at a tea stall in Cumilla last night.
The incident occurred around 10:50 PM in the Dhanpur area of Adarsha Sadar upazila, while viewers were watching the Argentina-Egypt FIFA World Cup match.
According to police, an argument broke out after Argentina captain Lionel Messi missed a penalty during the game.
The clash turned violent, and two local men, identified as Babu and Main Uddin Malu, allegedly struck Shariful on the head.
Locals rescued the victim and rushed him to Cumilla Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
Police have visited the scene and sent the body to the hospital morgue for an autopsy.
Cumilla Kotwali Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Touhidul Anwar stated that police are conducting raids to identify and detain the suspects.
As of 10:00 AM today, no arrests have been made and no formal murder case has been filed.
caption:
A football argument over a missed penalty by Lionel Messi turned fatal in Cumilla.

A 35-year-old man, identified as Md Shariful Islam, was killed after a dispute among football supporters escalated into violence at a tea stall in Cumilla last night.

The incident occurred around 10:50 PM in the Dhanpur area of Adarsha Sadar upazila, while viewers were watching the Argentina-Egypt FIFA World Cup match.

According to police, an argument broke out after Argentina captain Lionel Messi missed a penalty during the game.

The clash turned violent, and two local men, identified as Babu and Main Uddin Malu, allegedly struck Shariful on the head.

Locals rescued the victim and rushed him to Cumilla Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

Police have visited the scene and sent the body to the hospital morgue for an autopsy.

Cumilla Kotwali Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Touhidul Anwar stated that police are conducting raids to identify and detain the suspects.

As of 10:00 AM today, no arrests have been made and no formal murder case has been filed.
